Section I: Program Overview & Background 1.1 Purpose The Department of the Air Force (DAF), Business and Enterprise Systems (BES) Directorate, AFLCMC/GBGD, is issuing this Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to identify and acquire an innovative, commercially available Digital Adoption Platform (DAP). This platform will replace the legacy Oracle User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. User Productivity Kit (UPK), which is reaching its official end-of-life. The primary goal of this acquisition is to secure a modern, sustainable, enterprise-ready software-guided training and performance-support tool. It must streamline content creation, simplify software adoption, and provide real-time in-application guidance for the DEAMS user base. 1.2 Mission Impact & Capability Gap The current solution (Oracle UPK) represents unsupported software and significant technical debt. Its retirement creates a critical operational gap in how training is conducted across the enterprise. The replacement DAP will modernize training material outputs, provide interactive in-application assistance, and reduce the overall training footprint. This capability is designated as a Criticality (1) — Must Have requirement to support continuous financial and enterprise operations. 1.3 Scope of the Target Environment • User Base: Approximately 26,000+ geographically dispersed personnel across 170+ global locations. • Primary Integration: Stable and proven integration with Oracle e-Business Suite (EBS) (including F orms & OAF pages) and modern web applications. • Target Environments: The DAP must be deployable and tested across both Development (Dev) and Test environments before transitioning to

The purpose of this system is to detect anomalies in real-time through comparison of historical process conditions and real-time information; and also provide the means for users to access this data; to display high-quality graphics; plot and trend this data; and provide notification of equipment performance anomalies. The anomaly detection system must be designed to accommodate very large real-time and historical databases so that multiple anomaly detection models can be run simultaneously. The models must be scalable and efficient so that they can run at any interval up to once every 1 minute, as required by the end user. The results of all calculations must be stored on-line for years, in its original resolution preferably within Reclamation’s historian. The archive results must not in any way affect the calculated data from its original resolution and sampled state. With this high-resolution data available, users can view both the plant conditions and analytic results while providing a very clear and accurate picture of past operations. The system must also provide a method for managing and dispositioning alarms. Any dispositioned alarm should be easily accessible; users should be able to bring up a full analytic copy of all alarm information associated with a dispositioned alarm.
